value.body: Drone engineers design, build and test unmanned aircraft and their systems: airframes, propulsion, flight controllers, sensors and payloads. Employers include drone start-ups, defence and agriculture-drone makers, and survey firms. Work moves between CAD, the workshop and the test field.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E. in Aerospace, Mechanical or Electronics

items.label: Common tools
items.value: CAD software, flight-control firmware (e.g. PX4, ArduPilot), test rigs

items.label: Rules that apply
items.note: Cover drone certification, registration and remote pilot certificates

items.label: Registered drones (UINs issued)
items.note: Issued on the Digital Sky platform

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Drone companies often hire from student drone and aeromodelling clubs, competitions and internships. A portfolio of drones built or flown, and a DGCA remote pilot certificate, can help at interviews.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many employers are start-ups, so roles can be broad and change quickly.
Common next steps: senior UAV engineer, systems lead, or test and certification roles.
Field testing can mean travel and outdoor work.
